claim: Baghdad founded by Abbasid Caliph al-Mansur in 762 CE as Madinat al-Salam
claim_ar: تأسيس بغداد على يد الخليفة العباسي المنصور سنة 762م باسم مدينة السلام
notes: Commonly cited founding year 762 CE (145 AH).

claim: Baghdad became a major intellectual/cultural center of the Islamic world during Abbasid era
claim_ar: أصبحت بغداد مركزًا فكريًا وثقافيًا رئيسيًا في العالم الإسلامي خلال العصر العباسي
notes: Broadly supported; avoid absolute superlatives without qualification.

claim: Buyid dynasty took control of Baghdad in 945 CE, reducing caliphal political power
claim_ar: سيطر البويهيون على بغداد سنة 945م، مما قلّص السلطة السياسية للخليفة
notes: Useful as a turning-point marker in timeline.

claim: House of Wisdom (Bayt al-Hikma) associated with Abbasid translation movement, especially under al-Ma'mun
claim_ar: بيت الحكمة ارتبط بحركة الترجمة العباسية، ولا سيما في عهد المأمون
source: Gutas, Greek Thought Arabic Culture; Jim Al-Khalili; Encyclopaedia sources
notes: Historians debate its exact institutional form (library/academy/bureau). Do not portray as a single modern-style university building without nuance.

claim: Translation movement rendered Greek, Persian, and Indian works into Arabic and stimulated original scholarship
claim_ar: حركة الترجمة نقلت أعمالًا يونانية وفارسية وهندية إلى العربية وأدت إلى إنتاج علمي أصيل
source: Dimitri Gutas; standard histories of science
notes: Name representative translators carefully (Hunayn ibn Ishaq, Thabit ibn Qurra etc.) only when sourced.

claim: Al-Ma'mun ruled 813-833 CE and patronized scholarship/translation
claim_ar: حكم المأمون 813–833م ورعى العلم والترجمة

claim: Mongol siege of Baghdad began late January 1258 and city fell in February 1258
claim_ar: بدأ حصار بغداد المغولي أواخر يناير 1258 وسقطت المدينة في فبراير 1258
notes: Siege operations reported around 29 Jan; surrender/fall around 10 Feb; sack followed.

claim: Hulagu Khan led the Mongol campaign that captured Baghdad
claim_ar: قاد هولاكو خان الحملة المغولية التي استولت على بغداد

claim: Caliph al-Musta'sim was the last Abbasid caliph in Baghdad and was executed after the fall
claim_ar: الخليفة المستعصم كان آخر خلفاء بني العباس في بغداد وأُعدم بعد السقوط
source: Standard accounts; details of method vary
notes: Method of execution differs across sources (carpet/trampling vs other reports). Avoid stating one method as certain.

claim: Death toll of Baghdad 1258 is highly uncertain and varies widely across sources
claim_ar: عدد قتلى سقوط بغداد 1258 غير مؤكد ويختلف اختلافًا كبيرًا بين المصادر
source: Hulagu letter reports ~200,000; later chronicles report 800,000-2,000,000; modern reassessments often lower/uncertain
notes: DO NOT present a single number as fact. Script must say estimates vary widely and are disputed.

claim: Claims that Tigris ran black with ink from books are widely reported but of debated historicity
claim_ar: الرواية التي تقول إن دجلة اسودّ من حبر الكتب منتشرة لكن تاريخيتها محل نقاش
source: Later chronicles; Michal Biran et al. note exaggeration/legend elements; some manuscripts/libraries survived
notes: May be used only as a reported tradition, clearly framed as 'تروي بعض الروايات...' not as confirmed physical measurement.

claim: Libraries and books were destroyed/damaged during the sack, but destruction was not total; some collections survived
claim_ar: تعرّضت مكتبات وكتب للتدمير/الضرر أثناء السقوط، لكن الدمار لم يكن كليًا وبقيت بعض المجموعات
source: Roper, Muslim Heritage; Michal Biran; evidence of surviving manuscripts
notes: Avoid absolute 'all knowledge destroyed'. Say 'خسارة هائلة' with nuance.

claim: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi was associated with Hulagu and later Maragha observatory; claims he saved 400,000 books before siege are popular but poorly documented in strong primary sources
claim_ar: نصير الدين الطوسي ارتبط بهولاكو ثم بمرصد مراغة؛ أما ادعاء إنقاذه 400 ألف كتاب قبل الحصار فشائع لكنه ضعيف التوثيق في مصادر أولية قوية
source: Popular retellings; some modern articles repeat claim; strong primary corroboration not established in reviewed sources
notes: Do NOT state 400,000 as fact. If mentioned at all, frame as unverified popular claim or omit.

claim: Maragha observatory was established after 1258 under Ilkhanate patronage with Tusi's involvement
claim_ar: أُسس مرصد مراغة بعد 1258 برعاية الإيلخانيين وبمشاركة الطوسي
source: Encyclopaedia Iranica; history of astronomy sources
notes: Date often given 1259 for construction start; keep precise dating careful.

claim: Baghdad's political/intellectual centrality declined after 1258 though city continued to exist
claim_ar: تراجعت المكانة السياسية والفكرية المركزية لبغداد بعد 1258 رغم استمرار المدينة

claim: Mongols spared some communities in some accounts (e.g., Christians who took refuge) — varies by source
claim_ar: تذكر بعض الروايات أن المغول استثنوا بعض الجماعات، لكن ذلك يختلف باختلاف المصادر
notes: Do not make blanket claims without specific sourced detail.

claim: Mustansiriya school was founded 1227 CE in Baghdad and survived as an institution in some form after Mongol period
claim_ar: المدرسة المستنصرية أُسست في بغداد سنة 1227م واستمرت بشكل ما بعد الحقبة المغولية

claim: Yaqut al-Hamawi (1179-1229) wrote Mu'jam al-Buldan praising Baghdad
claim_ar: ياقوت الحموي (1179–1229) كتب معجم البلدان وفيه وصف لبغداد
notes: Quote used in example must be verified against text/translation before final VO.

claim: The quote 'Baghdad was the heart of Iraq...' attributed to Yaqut in the showcase is plausible in theme but exact Arabic wording must be verified from Mu'jam al-Buldan
claim_ar: الاقتباس المنسوب لياقوت في العرض الترويجي معقول المعنى لكن صياغته العربية الدقيقة يجب التحقق منها من معجم البلدان
notes: Do not lock script on exact wording until verified against source edition.

claim: No credible historical source can quantify 'lives saved' by a counterfactual Baghdad not falling
claim_ar: لا يوجد مصدر تاريخي موثوق يمكنه قياس 'أرواح أُنقذت' في سيناريو افتراضي لعدم سقوط بغداد
notes: Hard no: never claim number of lives saved/lost by counterfactual.
